construct: Left ventricular coronary perfusion occurs predominantly during diastole. Coronary perfusion pressure is approximated by aortic diastolic pressure minus left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (CPP = ADP − LVEDP). A rise in LVEDP therefore decreases the driving gradient for coronary flow and can particularly compromise subendocardial perfusion.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Left-ventricular coronary perfusion is driven mainly during diastole by the gradient from aortic diastolic pressure to LV end-diastolic pressure; acute elevation of LVEDP narrows this gradient.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Mean arterial pressure minus right atrial pressure is a legitimate systemic perfusion concept and therefore the strongest formula distractor, but it does not define left-ventricular coronary perfusion pressure.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only aortic diastolic pressure minus LVEDP is the pressure relationship both altered by the stem and directly linked to subendocardial coronary flow.
